title: The Great Commission
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The Great Commission is Christ’s command for His people to make disciples of all nations, baptizing them and teaching them to obey all He commanded. It rests on His authority and His promised presence.
summary: The Great Commission is Christ’s command for His people to make disciples of all nations, baptizing them and teaching them to obey all He commanded. It rests on His authority and His promised presence.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the risen Lord who sends His people. Because all authority belongs to Him, the church goes with His message, under His command, and with confidence in His presence.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Great Commission begins with Christ’s authority. The church does not invent its mission. The risen Lord commands His people to go, make disciples, baptize, and teach obedience.

Disciple-making includes evangelism but does not stop there. Those who believe are to be baptized and taught to observe all that Christ commanded. The goal is not merely decisions, but formed followers of Jesus.

This commission extends to all nations. Christ’s Gospel crosses ethnic, cultural, language, social, and geographic boundaries because He is Lord over all.

Jesus also promises His presence. The church goes not in self-confidence, but in reliance on the Lord who says He is with His people always, even to the end of the age.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some believers think mission belongs only to pastors, missionaries, or unusually gifted people. The Great Commission belongs to the church under the authority of Christ.

This doctrine also corrects shallow evangelism. Jesus commanded His people to make disciples, not merely attract attention or count responses. The church must proclaim, baptize, teach, and walk with people toward obedience.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Take Christ’s commission personally and as part of His church. Pray for the nations and your neighbors, speak the Gospel clearly, support faithful mission, and help others learn to obey Jesus. Do not separate evangelism from discipleship or mission from the authority of Christ.
